paper_metadata.title: Enhanced high temperature mechanical properties and heat resistance of an Al–Cu–Mg–Fe–Ni matrix composite reinforced with in-situ TiB2 particles

evidence.quote: In this work, TiB2 nanoparticles were in-situ introduced to a typical heat resistant Al–Cu–Mg–Fe–Ni (Al2618) alloy matrix and subjected to hot extrusion.

process_steps.input_state: molten pure Al with K2TiF6 and KBF4 salts

evidence.quote: An Al–TiB2 master alloy was initially fabricated by adding high-purity reactive salts (≥ 99.0%) of K2TiF6 and KBF4 into the molten pure Al (99.99%) in a high-purity graphite crucible using an electrical resistance furnace at 900 °C. The melt was mechanically stirred at a rotation speed of 600 rpm for 15 min.
After slag removal, the melt was cast in a graphite mould to obtain the Al–TiB 2 master alloy.

The introduction of TiB2 particles on one hand refined the grain size, providing grain refinement accordingly.
TiB2 particles provide load bearing strengthening effect by transferring loading from Al matrix, which enhances the yield strength of the composite.
In addition, the submicron-sized TiB2 particles can act as obstacles to inhibit the dislocation migration via the Orowan effect and result in an increase of YS.
Owing to the mismatch in thermal expansion coefficients between TiB2 and Al matrix, the dislocation density in the matrix is increased, leading to the strengthening of the composite.
In the subsequent thermal exposure, the growth of the fine grains is limited by the TiB2 particle bands.
